group.title: Nuanced adverbs
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Without meaning to, by accident.
examples: I {inadvertently} deleted the file.
wrong: She inadvertently planned the surprise down to every detail.

words.meaning: With careful, deliberate effort.
examples: He {studiously} avoided looking at his ex-partner.
wrong: She studiously ignored the email by reading it at once.

words.meaning: In a way that cannot be avoided or escaped.
examples: The plot moves {ineluctably} toward tragedy.
wrong: The result followed ineluctably, though it could easily have been avoided.

words.meaning: In a way that can never be changed or undone.
examples: The decision {irrevocably} altered their lives.
wrong: The contract was irrevocably signed, so we canceled it the next day.

words.meaning: Quickly and with little care or interest, just as a duty.
examples: The guard {perfunctorily} glanced at my ticket.
wrong: She checked the report perfunctorily, going over every line twice.

words.meaning: With great care and constant hard work.
examples: She {assiduously} checked every reference.
wrong: He worked assiduously, giving up after ten minutes.

words.meaning: In an unwilling or resentful way.
examples: He {begrudgingly} admitted that she was right.
wrong: She begrudgingly agreed, smiling with delight.

words.meaning: By a long, indirect route or way.
examples: The road winds {circuitously} through the hills.
wrong: He answered circuitously, getting straight to the point.

words.meaning: In a way that can be clearly shown or proved.
examples: The claim is {demonstrably} false.
wrong: The idea was demonstrably true, yet there was no proof at all.

words.meaning: Too much or too little compared with something else.
examples: Poorer areas are {disproportionately} affected by pollution.
wrong: The cost fell disproportionately, shared equally by everyone.

words.meaning: For a very short time.
examples: She smiled {fleetingly} before turning away.
wrong: He glanced fleetingly at the painting for three hours.

words.meaning: Without order, plan or care.
examples: Books were piled {haphazardly} on the floor.
wrong: The files were arranged haphazardly, in perfect alphabetical order.

words.meaning: So slowly or slightly that it can hardly be noticed.
examples: The light faded {imperceptibly} into evening.
wrong: The noise rose imperceptibly into a deafening crash everyone heard.

words.meaning: In an indirect way, not stated openly.
examples: She referred only {obliquely} to the scandal.
wrong: He mentioned it obliquely, naming the problem loudly and clearly.

words.meaning: With very great care and attention to detail.
examples: The old mural was {painstakingly} restored.
wrong: She painstakingly finished the model in a careless rush.

words.meaning: In an unsafe, unstable way that might fall or fail.
examples: The vase was balanced {precariously} on the edge.
wrong: The tower stood precariously, firm and completely safe.

words.meaning: By a lucky, unplanned chance.
examples: We met {serendipitously} at a train station in Lisbon.
wrong: They met serendipitously, after months of careful planning.

words.meaning: Immediately and without the usual process or discussion.
examples: He was {summarily} dismissed for misconduct.
wrong: The case was summarily decided after a three-year trial.

words.meaning: Secretly, so that others don’t notice.
examples: He {surreptitiously} checked his phone during the meeting.
wrong: She surreptitiously waved a flag in front of everyone.

words.meaning: Without knowing or realizing.
examples: She {unwittingly} revealed the surprise.
wrong: He unwittingly broke the rule he had carefully planned to break.

words.meaning: By sharing someone else’s experience through imagination.
examples: He travels {vicariously} through his daughter’s letters.
wrong: She lived vicariously through her friend by climbing the mountain herself.

words.meaning: In a dry, slightly mocking or ironic way.
examples: ’Another perfect day,’ she said {wryly} as the rain poured.
wrong: He smiled wryly, with completely sincere and innocent joy.

words.meaning: Without any doubt.
examples: This is {indubitably} the finest wine of the year.
wrong: It was indubitably true, though most people strongly doubted it.

words.meaning: Openly, without shame or embarrassment.
examples: He is {unabashedly} romantic.
wrong: She sang unabashedly, hiding her face in shame.

words.meaning: Much more than is usual or reasonable.
examples: She was {inordinately} proud of her small garden.
wrong: The meal was inordinately expensive at a perfectly normal price.

words.meaning: By lucky chance.
examples: The rain stopped {fortuitously} just before the wedding.
wrong: It happened fortuitously, exactly as we had arranged.

words.meaning: Very carefully and slowly, to avoid harm or pain.
examples: She stepped {gingerly} onto the icy path.
wrong: He gingerly kicked the fragile glass across the room.

words.meaning: Quickly and without stopping to think.
examples: They rushed {headlong} into the deal.
wrong: She went headlong into it after months of careful thought.

words.meaning: As fast as possible.
examples: The documents were sent {posthaste} to the lawyer.
wrong: He replied posthaste, three months later.

words.meaning: In a way that cannot be explained.
examples: The lights {inexplicably} went out.
wrong: It failed inexplicably, for a reason everyone understood.

words.meaning: In a way that cannot be denied or argued against.
examples: The tests {incontrovertibly} proved his innocence.
wrong: The evidence was incontrovertibly clear, so the debate continued for years.

words.meaning: In a firm, determined way that does not change.
examples: She {resolutely} refused to sign.
wrong: He resolutely changed his mind every few minutes.

words.meaning: Now and then, at irregular times.
examples: Fighting continued {sporadically} through the night.
wrong: It rained sporadically, without a single pause all week.

words.meaning: Later than should have happened.
examples: The company {belatedly} admitted the fault.
wrong: She belatedly sent the card a week early.

words.meaning: In name only, not in reality.
examples: He is {nominally} in charge, but his deputy makes the decisions.
wrong: She was nominally the boss and truly made every decision.

words.meaning: In a commanding way that allows no refusal or discussion.
examples: ’Sit down,’ he said {peremptorily}.
wrong: She peremptorily asked if we might perhaps consider sitting.

words.meaning: Calmly and fairly, without letting feelings influence you.
examples: A judge must weigh the evidence {dispassionately}.
wrong: He spoke dispassionately, shouting with rage.

words.meaning: In small steps, one after another.
examples: Prices rose {incrementally} over the decade.
wrong: The system was improved incrementally, all at once in a single leap.

words.meaning: In a careless way that ignores how serious something is.
examples: He {cavalierly} dismissed the safety warnings.
wrong: She treated the risk cavalierly, studying it with great care.

words.meaning: Loudly and forcefully, especially in complaint.
examples: Fans protested {vociferously} against the ticket prices.
wrong: They objected vociferously in total silence.
